CapturedAuthorizationAuthority.broker_issued_exactness: The authority broker alone registers an exact final concrete instance during construction. held_dependencies.contract: _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract only prepares and verifies an immutable batch from a fixed resolver snapshot. It cannot reserve/consume/abort admissions, write/lookup a ledger, construct sessions/events, open members/providers, import, construct, execute, output, invoke a callback, or spend authority.
held_dependencies.resolver: The held WORM resolver owns one immutable snapshot and recursively verifies the selected admission, all ADR-defined signed artifacts, IssuanceBasis.v1 and exact references with shared local validators: canonical grammar, named self, SHA-256, Ed25519, role/use, trusted time, revocation, closed basis/ref sets, cycles, future output and action/replay adjacency. The P4 contract never interprets their externally owned application schemas or treats unresolved bytes as verified. No request selects bytes beyond copied fixture facts, a generation, path, URL, fallback, store, resolver, callback or trust root.
held_dependencies.integrity: Before preparation and again inside the sole transition lock before commit, the authority verifies exact private dependency identities/classes, immutable construction commitments, broker attestation, and final dispatch capsule. Dependencies expose no getter and retain only copied frozen state. Any mismatch, replacement, unexpected result, or altered commitment refuses before preparation or ledger entry. These checks include the held terminal-verifier/policy/dispatch identities, the snapshot's exact root and generation, every anchor issuance registration and all opaque binding commitments. Anchor currentness is revalidated inside the sole transition lock before commit; an earlier cached verification cannot authorize a stale generation.

HistoricalStudyVerifier.constructor: HistoricalStudyVerifier(authority) remains the existing LifecycleAuthority constructor: it accepts any valid isinstance(authority, LifecycleAuthority), identity-pins that exact authority, and neither constructs nor upgrades it. bind and capture remain unchanged and ordinary v1 capture remains available through the held v1 authority.

M02_to_M08_retained_transaction.legacy: Validate outside and inside the shared lock; atomically transition PUBLISHED through LEGACY_COMMITTING to CAPTURED_V1 while appending the v1 receipt, binding/interning the legacy session, and recording its sole start identity. Later P4 sees CAPTURED_V1 and refuses before P4 reservation/batch/session/admission effect.
M02_to_M08_retained_transaction.p4: The fixed contract resolves and prepares/verifies without authority effect. Under the same lock, recheck exact PUBLISHED heads, unused nonces/admission, absent key, dependency commitments, fixed snapshot, complete field adjacency, frozen live projection, broker attestation, and dispatch capsule. The one immutable commit first consumes the admission, then publishes/mints the complete verified port/receipt/set/replay batch, session identity, and atomic SessionStartRecord, then transitions all identities to P4_COMMITTED without releasing the lock. The under-lock recheck includes terminal root/policy/snapshot/anchor commitments, validity and verification-generation currentness. A stale or revoked anchor rejects the entire batch before consumption, never by partially committing or later rolling back a WORM admission.
M02_to_M08_retained_transaction.resolver_and_basis: The held recursive resolver retains full ADR-0125 basis closure: P(CES)==P(BVP)==P(CAS)==P(StageAdmission or FinalReplayEntry)==ordered PlannedCaptureSet==ordered live captures by complete PCE bytes/cardinality, with exact action/replay admission, signer/use, time, revocation, self/preimage, predecessor-publication, port/receipt/set, replay-evidence, and session-decision adjacency. For the two external families, this closure additionally requires the complete exact terminal anchor set and authenticated parent/publication-policy linkage under the same snapshot. An anchor is not a CaptureAdmissionSet, execution admission, port authorization, receipt, session or consumption authority.
M02_to_M08_retained_transaction.failure_retry_race: Preparation, verification, dependency, fixture, trust, mutation, or precommit failure leaves heads PUBLISHED and admission UNUSED; only lock-private reservation is discarded and a corrected retry is legal. The commit publishes one complete record or nothing. An uncertain post-boundary caller resolves exact key/admission before any remint. Legacy/P4 races serialize on the one lock; all listed capture/open/bind/member/consume/release routes refuse for P4_RESERVING/P4_COMMITTED matched identities before effect, while unrelated ordinary v1 remains positive. A failed or stale terminal proof leaves the admission UNUSED and live heads PUBLISHED. A corrected retry obtains a fresh complete closure from the held current snapshot; it cannot reuse a stale anchor, bypass full local verification or remint after an uncertain committed outcome.
M02_to_M08_retained_transaction.prepared_and_session: Prepared bytes are private, inaccessible, nonserializable, and nonauthoritative until same-ledger publication. Session identity/nonce and canonical SessionStartRecord are fields of the same committed record; postcommit opaque interning/return cannot mint another session or event. This preserves M02-M08 without claiming durable/restart consume-once closure.

No lifecycle method or facade accepts this capability as an argument.
methods: verify_terminal(snapshot, parent_basis_bytes, terminal_class, terminal_ref_bytes, canonical_artifact_bytes) -> VerifiedExternalArtifactAnchor
TerminalArtifactVerifier.method_inputs: These methods are called only by the fixed resolver/contract using its held opaque snapshot, already locally verified exact canonical IssuanceBasis bytes, derived terminal class/position, exact four-key ref bytes, and bytes resolved from that same snapshot. No path, URL, callback, generation, policy, trust root, clock, verifier, key or result override is accepted. require_current accepts only an exact tuple of the same issuer's registered anchors and never issues an anchor or spends authority.
TerminalArtifactVerifier.method_results: verify_terminal either returns one exact registered anchor after external owner/signature/key-use/time/revocation/policy verification or raises. None, boolean, dict, bytes, unsigned marker, alias to a different anchor, subclass, unexpected result or missing verification identity refuses. require_current raises on any stale/revoked/substituted anchor; None means only all requested anchors remain valid at the held trusted check.

VerifiedExternalArtifactAnchor.kind: Opaque nonconstructible final value issued only by the registered terminal authority; exported as a type, with no public data constructor, getters, bytes/dict/mapping/iteration/path/member access, callable behavior, copy/deepcopy/pickle/reduce/getstate/setstate or deserialization.
private_bindings: exact issuing terminal-verifier identity and immutable dispatch attestation
exact broker identity and trust-root identity
exact immutable resolver snapshot object and snapshot content commitment
exact canonical IssuanceBasisRef.v1 four-key bytes and its ref.sha256 artifact identity
SHA-256 of the exact canonical external bytes resolved from that snapshot, independently of the artifact's externally defined named digest
closed terminal class: G1-dataset-authorization, G2-dataset-authorization, or fixed-owner-policy
exact parent IssuanceBasis identity/kind and permitted terminal position
external policy identity and authenticated publication/policy subject linkage
verified signer/owner identity, exclusive key usage, key ID/version and signature-verification identity
trusted verification instant, validity interval and immutable authenticated revocation-verification identity
terminal verification generation and snapshot generation
VerifiedExternalArtifactAnchor.authentication: All bindings are issuer-owned frozen commitments, not fields asserted by the fixture or caller. The issuer externally validates both the named artifact identity and the canonical-bytes digest according to the owning policy. The local contract checks exact anchor issuance identity, all requested bindings and currentness through broker-held checked dispatch; object type or digest equality alone never establishes trust.

methods: _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract.prepare_batch(snapshot, captures, admission_ref, runtime) -> private prepared batch
private_composition.construction: The one private _development_p4_broker(*, fixture_facts=None) constructs and registers the exact graph internally. Dependencies are privately held, have no getter, and expose no mutable policy/corpus/registry/table or reconstruction API. No alternate factory argument, opt-in on _development_broker, late registration or facade upgrade can introduce a verifier or anchor.
private_composition.unavailable: Absent external terminal authority, absent trusted policy binding, missing external authentication/linkage, unknown terminal class or unsupported verifier state fails closed before preparation/ledger/session effects. There is no synthetic or local-signature fallback in a deployment context.

closed_terminal_routing.selection: The resolver first classifies an exact ref by its already verified parent basis kind and fixed expected reference projection. An ADR-defined schema always uses its local validator. An external terminal position is available only when the broker-held external policy already binds its exact four-key ref identity, expected terminal class and parent subject; ref.schema alone never chooses the terminal route. Literal external schema identifiers are opaque policy-bound identities, not new DSKit artifact schemas or wildcard allowances.

routes.cardinality: Exactly one verified G1 anchor and one verified G2 anchor for the root-PIS authorization subject, plus the complete exact local root-publication-receipt ref projection. Neither one alone, two of one class, an extra anchor, missing receipt, unrelated authorization or duplicate complete ref is valid.
routes.requirements: G1 and G2 are independently verified as their respective dataset-authorization terminal classes under the fixed external policy, including that policy's authenticated owner, signer and exclusive authorized key-use requirements. This seam does not assign the ADR GateEvidenceRef security-gate/data-gate uses to the externally specified dataset authorizations or invent their production key-use identifiers. The two anchors must authenticate the same exact dataset authorization subject and the publication_authorization_ref of each relevant locally verified RootPublicationReceipt. The parent basis refs and the PIS receipt/entry projection must match completely.

routes.cardinality: The same exact G1/G2 authorization references and authenticated owner approvals required by its parent root-PIS are checked for the root receipt's existing dataset-capture publication_authorization_ref. Each parent use requires its own correctly parent-bound opaque anchors within the same immutable snapshot; an anchor issued for another parent cannot be substituted. This links the same two approvals without creating a new terminal class, unsigned receipt fallback or fresh dataset authorization.
routes.requirements: The local root-receipt validator verifies its full ADR-0125 schema, self, signature, basis and root/producer/member facts. Only the externally owned authorization behind its dataset-capture tag is terminal; both approvals must bind that tag and those declared publication facts.

routes.cardinality: Exactly one fixed-owner-policy anchor plus the exact locally verified root-PIS reference; no extra/missing policy or local-artifact substitution.
routes.requirements: The anchor authenticates the one broker-selected owner policy identity and the ScopeIntent's complete policy-covered study/environment/profile/component/candidate/policy/closed-intent projection. Digest-only equality, a different study policy, a gate-derived policy or a policy referring to future execution output refuses.

closed_terminal_routing.all_other_positions: No other basis kind/position permits an external terminal. In particular PEA, CES, BVP, CAS, ScopeAuthorization, GateEvidenceRef, StageAdmission, ActionExecutionAdmission, stage publications, final manifest, FinalReplayAdmission, capture artifacts and replay evidence cannot become terminals because a local schema or link is absent.
closed_terminal_routing.dual_owner_linkage: The existing dataset-capture publication tag has one authorization digest; the resolver must not guess whether an external authority encodes G1/G2 as two signatures over one artifact or as linked owner approvals. The fixed external verification policy must authenticate both role-specific exact refs to that same tagged authorization subject. This linkage is part of the opaque anchors' private commitments. Missing or ambiguous linkage refuses. No new production wire representation for dual approval is defined by this matrix.
closed_terminal_routing.local_closure_retained: All local refs, all basis shapes/kinds/ref sets, canonical order and duplicate checks, signed self/preimage/key-use/time/revocation checks, predecessor-publication equality, BVP/PlannedCaptureSet payload and P(CES)==P(BVP)==P(CAS)==P(Stage or FinalReplayEntry)==ordered live capture equality remain mandatory. Cycles or future-output dependencies cannot be hidden behind an anchor; terminal policy attests the external object is a leaf for this closed authorization subject.
closed_terminal_routing.no_fallback: Unknown schema, unsupported schema version, absent local resolver entry, malformed canonical bytes, failed local signature/basis/currentness or unavailable terminal authority always refuses. Neither a fixture entry nor a permissive subclass can register a new terminal route.

synthetic_terminal_composition.scope: A fixed private synthetic terminal verifier provides nondeployment test authority only. Its acceptance corpus, signer keys/roles/uses, trusted time, revocation policy, external policy identity and verification-generation rules are construction-owned constants. They cannot be selected or overridden by fixture data.

fixture_grammar.outer: None (empty facts) or exact built-in dict with only artifacts
fixture_grammar.artifacts: exact built-in list of exact built-in dicts with only ref and bytes
fixture_grammar.ref: exact IssuanceBasisRef.v1 dict with only kind, role, schema, sha256; all exact strings, valid nonplaceholder lowercase SHA-256
fixture_grammar.bytes: exact built-in canonical JSON bytes, copied and retained once; no application-specific external schema is inferred
fixture_grammar.closed_loading: Every local artifact is classified by the fixed local schema/ref policy. Only the exact broker-policy-pinned external references can be offered at their closed terminal positions. Unknown fields, aliases/cycles, duplicate refs or complete items, subclasses, Mapping/Sequence impostors, callables, handles, paths/URLs, stores and noncanonical bytes refuse. The outer source is recursively copied, and post-return source mutation cannot alter the snapshot.
fixture_grammar.compatibility: This widens the existing foundation loader's admission-only artifact inventory only after a clean v8 verdict; it does not change the private factory signature or the public authorize_capture_set signatures.

synthetic_terminal_composition.fixed_positive_evidence: The private synthetic verifier holds an independently authenticated fixed external test corpus and role/policy bindings, including valid G1/G2 and owner-policy cases. Submitted bytes and exact refs must match that corpus and pass the fixed external verification policy before anchor issuance. It must not bless arbitrary bytes by hashing them, echoing their ref, signing them with a test key, or accepting a caller's verified flag. The corpus is test data for an external format, not a DSKit production artifact schema. Invalid, expired, revoked, wrong-owner/use and tampered corpus variants must fail against independently pinned expected outcomes.
synthetic_terminal_composition.snapshots: The resolver constructs one private immutable snapshot from copied artifacts and the fixed trusted policy/root commitment. Snapshot identity/content/generation are internally chosen; callers cannot request or reconstruct a generation. Anchors never cross snapshots or brokers, even if canonical bytes/digests look equal. Snapshot content or verification-generation changes require fresh verification; cached prior anchors refuse.
synthetic_terminal_composition.private_attack_checks: Exact final verifier/policy/lookup/dispatch identities, registration and copied corpus commitments are checked before resolution and again inside the lifecycle transition lock before commit. One dependency/table/anchor/attestation/generation/class-method replacement must refuse or create no authority effect. Coordinated multiple-private rewrites remain ADR-0126-deferred; they are not offered as a real external security boundary.
synthetic_terminal_composition.chronology: Anchor verification itself is nonauthorizing evidence production. It emits no lifecycle receipt, admission consumption, batch, LaunchSession, SessionStartRecord, provider/member access, application import/construction/run/output or release. Partial anchor verification failure abandons that private closure; no partial anchor set can escape to a caller or later satisfy a different request.

terminal_freshness_and_atomicity.freshness: Both local and terminal trust checks use broker-held trusted time and authenticated immutable revocation state, never a request timestamp. Verification records its generation and validity; immediately before the one ledger publication, require_current checks every anchor against the same held root/policy/snapshot commitments and the broker's current trusted verification generation.
terminal_freshness_and_atomicity.ordering: The authority serializes acceptance of trusted snapshot/generation updates and the final currentness check with its capture-transition decision. If an accepted revocation/policy/generation update precedes that decision, stale prepared anchors refuse. A snapshot is never mutated in place to simulate freshness. This is the stated in-process decision order only, not a distributed revocation/crash-consistency promise.
terminal_freshness_and_atomicity.verification_only: The terminal verifier cannot hold a hidden spend callback or its own admission/session store. The only authoritative action remains the existing same-ledger consume-plus-complete-batch publication after full local and terminal verification. Terminal-proof interning is not admission reservation, consumption or a second lifecycle writer.
terminal_freshness_and_atomicity.refusal: External verification exception, unavailable policy, expiry, revoked key, wrong snapshot/generation, malformed/unregistered anchor, partial proof set, changed corpus/dispatch, no exact parent match or post-prepare substitution refuses before the logical commit. No terminal failure is softened to an unsigned marker or a later check.

threat_model.actors: Hostile application/fixture callers can supply closed data, alter their original data after factory return, call all public lifecycle/facade methods, pass forged/cross-broker handles and race operations. Only the held broker composition owns verification policy, snapshot/anchor issuance and lifecycle state.
threat_model.trusted_authorities: The fixed local signer/keyring/clock/revocation authorities and the new fixed external terminal-verification authority are trust roots, not caller choices. Each has an exact issued identity, registered final implementation and private dispatch commitment. The terminal root verifies external semantics; only LifecycleAuthority writes admission/capture/session state.
threat_model.single_surface: Retain ADR-0126's single public-API, one intern-map, one handle poke, receipt-store or recovery-check mutation model. Apply it to new terminal/snapshot/anchor/policy/dispatch surfaces as well. A single-substitution success that yields a genuine P4 authorization/session or advances CAS is in scope.
threat_model.deferred: Coordinated multiple-private/interpreter rewrites, deployment key compromise, OS-owned broker implementation, durable/restart and cross-process consume-once remain explicitly unproved. No theorem about malicious code with total interpreter control is claimed.

success_and_exit.phase0: A fresh independent design skeptic must approve this exact frozen v8 matrix with zero unresolved in-scope Critical/Major before new terminal/ref-closure RED or GREEN. The author cannot count 0084 as approval of this material delta.
success_and_exit.incremental: A closure-only increment may prove exact local/terminal verification and still refuse at the not-yet-implemented atomic issuance boundary, but must label that result incomplete and demonstrate valid-versus-invalid closure with meaningful distinct assertions. It cannot claim Packet 4 GREEN or hide absent writer/batch/session work.
success_and_exit.whole_packet: Only complete action/replay one/multi-PCE success, all local and external refusal families, exact v2 port/receipt/set/replay output, shared legacy/P4 arbitration, same-record admission/session-start commit, uncertainty resolution, v1 compatibility, required checks and two fresh independent final lenses can close the bounded Packet 4 candidate. R23/whole-F5a/deployment remain separate.
success_and_exit.migration: Once owning F3/G1/G2 or fixed-policy schemas are approved, replace the temporary opaque terminal composition only through a reviewed ownership/schema migration that preserves exact existing anchors/refs and refuses silent reinterpretation. No automatic promotion of synthetic corpus anchors to production authority is permitted.
